summary: The first statement of how the Network Working Group's notes should work. Anyone at any site could write a note, and notes were meant to be timely rather than polished, covering host software and other aspects of the network. This informal approach is the origin of the Request for Comments series. It was replaced by RFC 10.

plainLanguage.summary: RFC 3 sets conventions for Network Working Group notes about host software and the network. Anyone could write a note, and the group encouraged sharing ideas promptly rather than waiting for a polished document; RFC 10 later obsoleted this memo.

subtitle: The original conventions for sharing Network Working Group notes.

tldr.problem: The Network Working Group needed a way to share timely ideas about host software and other aspects of the network.
tldr.mechanism: The memo allows anyone at any site to write a note, encourages timely rather than polished content, and sets basic header and distribution conventions.

sections.title: Who Could Write a Note
sections.content: The Network Working Group was concerned with host software, strategies for using the network, and initial network experiments. Notes documenting this work could be produced at any site by anybody and included in the series.
sections.plainLanguage: Anyone at any site could write a note about host software or another network topic and submit it to the series.

sections.title: Content and Style
sections.content:
A note could contain any thought or suggestion related to host software or another aspect of the network. Notes were encouraged to be timely rather than polished. Philosophical positions without examples, implementation suggestions without background, and questions without attempted answers were all acceptable. The minimum length was one sentence.

The memo explains that this informality was intended to encourage exchange and discussion of ideas that were not authoritative and to reduce hesitation about publishing unpolished work.
sections.plainLanguage: A note did not have to be complete or polished. Even a question without an answer could be shared to encourage discussion.

sections.title: Format and Distribution
sections.content: Each note should identify the Network Working Group, its serial number, the author and affiliation, the date, and a title. Bill Duvall at SRI assigned serial numbers. One copy was sent from the author's site to the designated recipients listed in the memo, and local reproduction could be handled as needed.
sections.plainLanguage: Each note had a number, author, date, and title. One copy went to the listed recipients, and sites could reproduce it locally.
